title: QuoteRepair
description: Shape contract for the repair pass: the items of a dictated reading whose provenance FAILED, handed back to the model with the transcript, for one attempt at citing them properly. Not a second extraction — the reading is fixed, the sections are fixed, and the only thing in question is which span of the transcript each surviving item comes from and whether its text is a deletion of that span.

x-notes.whyThisExistsAtAll: src/core/profile.ts states that an extraction stays one-shot, because a follow-up turn that 'took the correction into account' would no longer be the thing the eval measures. This pass does not violate that rule; it is built to be the exception the rule permits, and the difference is where the trust sits. Nothing here is believed. Every repair is re-run through verifyQuote and verifyDerivation — the same functions, over the same pack rule, with no relaxation — and a repair that does not verify is DISCARDED, leaving the original item and its original failed verdict standing. The model is therefore allowed to propose a span and never allowed to certify one. What the pass can do is turn an item the verifier rejected into one the verifier accepts; what it cannot do is make anything look checked that is not.
x-notes.repairsNotItems: The output is a list of REPAIRS keyed to positions in a list the prompt numbers, not a reading. A pass free to emit items would be a second extraction wearing a different name: it could add a drug, drop a diagnosis, or move a finding between sections, and the eval's item recall would then be measuring two passes while reporting one. The applier refuses any index it did not ask about and any index twice, so the worst a malformed reply can do is repair nothing.
x-notes.propertyOrder: LOAD-BEARING, as in every schema in this pack: llama.cpp compiles properties into the grammar in the order given. `found` is emitted BEFORE `quote` so the model commits to whether the transcript supports this item at all before it starts writing a span. Reversed, the field would be a rubber stamp on whatever had just been produced — the model would write a quote and then be asked whether a quote exists, which is not a question anymore.
x-notes.foundFalseIsAnAnswer: `found: false` is the correct reply for an item the transcript genuinely does not support, and it is the reply this pass most needs to be able to give. An item the model invented cannot be repaired, only confessed; without this field the grammar would force a span to be produced for it, which is precisely how a hallucination acquires evidence. Nothing is deleted on a false — the item stays in the reading, still flagged, still unverified. Suppressing it would hide a fabrication from the one person able to judge it, and would quietly improve the hallucination count by removing the evidence rather than the fault.
x-notes.quoteStillNotCheckedBySchema: As in note-format.schema.json: no JSON Schema keyword can require a string to be a substring of the prompt, so `quote` is an ordinary string here and is verified AFTER decoding. That is the whole design of this pack repeated one level down — the grammar guarantees the shape of the proposal, the verifier guarantees its provenance, and this pass adds no third kind of authority.
x-notes.doseAlwaysPresent: `dose` is required and nullable on every repair, including repairs to items that have no dose, because a grammar branching on which section an item came from would have to encode that section in the reply — a second statement of something the index already says. The applier ignores `dose` for any item that is not a medication, so a model that fills it in on a history item changes nothing.
x-notes.cap46: 46 = the one presenting complaint plus the three 15-item arrays of note-format.schema.json. It is a bound on the reading this pass is repairing rather than a judgement about how many failures are reasonable: a transcript whose every item failed provenance is a real answer and must be expressible, because that is exactly the case a clinician most needs to see.

repairs.description: One entry per numbered item the prompt asked about, in the order it asked. An item you cannot fix is still an entry, with found false.

repair.description: One attempt at citing one item properly.

item.description: The number the prompt gave this item. An index outside the list, or one that appears twice, repairs nothing.

found.description: Whether the transcript contains a span that supports this item. False is a real and expected answer: an item nobody dictated cannot be cited, and saying so is better than producing a span for it.

quote.description: The span of the transcript this item comes from, copied character by character — widened or narrowed from the one that failed, never reworded. Ignored when found is false.

text.description: The item as a clinician should read it: the repaired quote with words DELETED. Ignored when found is false. May differ from the text that failed, because the point of the pass is that a text which introduced a word can be brought back inside a span that contains it.

dose.description: AMOUNT and FREQUENCY only, as the transcript says them, or null. Ignored entirely for any item that is not a medication.
